title: Check your understanding: The Three Main Areas of Git

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of the three main areas of git?
options: The working tree contains checked-out files, the index records the next snapshot to commit, and repository history stores committed snapshots. `git status`, `git diff` and `git diff --cached` expose different relationships between these areas.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: The working tree contains checked-out files, the index records the next snapshot to commit, and repository history stores committed snapshots. `git status`, `git diff` and `git diff --cached` expose different relationships between these areas.
questions.explanation: The working tree contains checked-out files, the index records the next snapshot to commit, and repository history stores committed snapshots. `git status`, `git diff` and `git diff --cached` expose different relationships between these areas.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git status --short` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with the three main areas of git?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
